parts.zh: 美国一名警察拦下了一辆在高速公路上行驶缓慢并跨车道漂移的大型SUV
澳大利亚昆士兰阳光海岸大学的最新科学研究表明
经营其中一家酒吧的Lesley Harper说这只猫深受顾客喜爱
正在组织Wilbur派对的Sarah Godfrey告诉当地报纸:"Wilbur是我们生活的一部分,对村里每个人来说都是如此。
M: 确实。还记得我们就是在那儿看到电影明星 Brigette Clark 的
W: 当然记得。我怎么可能忘记？当时一群人围着她要跟她合影
M: 那汉堡怎么样？去购物中心路上有家美式餐厅
W: 我喜欢那家店。他们的薯条很棒
W: 好啊。你问过 Jeremy 想不想跟我们一起去吗？
M: 我问过了。他说不行

items.stem: Why did the police officer stop the SUV car?

choices.text: He noticed the driver was too young to drive.
choices.zh: 他注意到驾驶员太年轻,不能开车。

choices.text: He found there was no one sitting at the wheel.
choices.zh: 他发现驾驶座上没有人。

choices.text: He thought something must be wrong with the driver.
choices.zh: 他认为驾驶员一定出了什么问题。

choices.text: He saw the driver changing lanes much too frequently.
choices.zh: 他看到驾驶员变换车道过于频繁。

items.stem: What did the boy tell the police officers he was planning to do?

choices.text: Buy a sports car.
Drive across town.
Leave California.
Visit his sister.

items.stem: What does the report say we have not yet understood about mobile phones?

choices.text: How they change the way we shop.
choices.zh: 手机如何改变我们的购物方式。

choices.text: How they alter human skeletons.
choices.zh: 手机如何改变人类骨骼。

choices.text: How they cause increased headaches.
choices.zh: 手机如何导致头痛增加。

choices.text: How they affect our communication.
choices.zh: 手机如何影响我们的沟通。

items.stem: What happens to the skin when rubbed or pressed constantly?

choices.text: It loosens.
It brightens.
It hardens.
It softens.

items.stem: What does the report say the village is going to do for the cat Wilbur?

choices.text: Create Internet pages for him.
Ask a local pet shop to adopt him.
Name an orange tree after him.
choices.zh: 用它的名字命名一棵橙树。

choices.text: Hold a birthday party for him.

items.stem: What do we learn from the report about the cat?

choices.text: He is a bold and aggressive pet.
choices.zh: 它是一只大胆好斗的宠物。

choices.text: He pays regular visits to village shops.
choices.zh: 它定期光顾村里的商店。

choices.text: He once bit a doctor's receptionist.
choices.zh: 它曾咬过一位医生的接待员。

choices.text: He likes to sit on the hairdresser's chair.
choices.zh: 它喜欢坐在理发师的椅子上。

items.stem: What does the pub owner, Lesley Harper, say about the cat?

choices.text: He is fond of luxury cat food.
He likes to stay in villagers' houses.
He knows everybody in the village.
He often seeks food around her pub.
choices.zh: 它经常在她的酒吧周围寻找食物。

items.stem: What are the speakers talking about in this conversation?

choices.text: Who to order the food.
Whether to have sandwiches.
When to go for their meal.
Where to have their lunch.

items.stem: Where did the speakers see Brigette Clark, the famous movie star?

choices.text: In the shopping center nearby.
In the expensive Italian style diner.
choices.zh: 在昂贵的意大利风格餐厅。

choices.text: At the Sandwich Place on Camden Street.
At the American restaurant they frequent.
choices.zh: 在他们常去的美式餐厅。

items.stem: Why does the woman say she needs to get back by 2:30?

choices.text: There is to be a conference call.
She has to meet with her boss then.
choices.zh: 她那时必须与老板会面。

choices.text: There will be crowds of people waiting for her.
She will have a photo taken with Brigette Clark.

items.stem: Why does the woman say Jeremy should throw his soup in the bin?

choices.text: She doesn't deem homemade soup tasty.
She doesn't think his wife cooks well.
choices.zh: 她认为他妻子厨艺不好。

choices.text: She feels Jeremy would rather dine out.
choices.zh: 她觉得Jeremy宁愿在外面吃饭。

choices.text: She has found the soup smells terrible.
choices.zh: 她发现这汤闻起来很难闻。

items.stem: Who is the man talking to in the conversation?

choices.text: A landlady.
A waitress.
A receptionist.
A saleswoman.

items.stem: What do we learn about the man's father-in-law from the conversation?

choices.text: He was involved in a terrible car accident last April.
choices.zh: 他去年四月遭遇了一场严重的车祸。

choices.text: He has much difficulty getting up and down stairs.
He is expected to undergo a knee operation.
choices.zh: 他预计要接受膝关节手术。

choices.text: He prefers to stay next door to the children.
choices.zh: 他更愿意住在孩子们隔壁。

items.stem: Why does the man say they will explore all the options available?

choices.text: To please his parents-in-law.
To find the best trip for his kids.
choices.zh: 为了给他的孩子们找到最好的旅行。

choices.text: To satisfy his curiosity.
To compare prices.

items.stem: What does the woman suggest the man and his family do close to the end of the conversation?

choices.text: Visit a local art gallery.
Go on a boat trip.
Take some photos of the islands.
Try her hand-made clothing.
choices.zh: 试穿她手工制作的衣服。

items.stem: What does the passage say about artificial intelligence agents?

choices.text: They are more intelligent than many of us.
choices.zh: 它们比我们许多人更聪明。

choices.text: They have already become our new friends.
choices.zh: 它们已经成为我们的新朋友。

choices.text: They have begun to affect our social behavior.
choices.zh: 它们已经开始影响我们的社会行为。

choices.text: They play increasingly more important roles.
choices.zh: 它们发挥着越来越重要的作用。

items.stem: What does the new study want to find out about using an artificial intelligence agent?

choices.text: Whether it might have any effect on the way we negotiate.
choices.zh: 它是否可能对我们谈判的方式产生影响。

choices.text: Whether it might actually outperform human negotiators.
choices.zh: 它是否可能实际上超越人类谈判者。

choices.text: Whether it can facilitate business transactions.
Whether it can speed up legal procedures.

items.stem: What did participants tend to do when assigned an AI agent to negotiate on their behalf?

choices.text: Choose to be tough.
Sympathize with their opponent.
Use deceptive strategies.
Appear to be pleasant.

items.stem: What do we learn about the benefits the participants gained from the healthy cooking course?

choices.text: They were perceived differently by some academics.
choices.zh: 它们被一些学者以不同方式看待。

choices.text: They still existed six months after the course ended.
choices.zh: 它们在课程结束六个月后仍然存在。

choices.text: They varied greatly among the course participants.
choices.zh: 它们在课程参与者之间差异很大。

choices.text: They were only measurable within seven weeks.
choices.zh: 它们只能在七周内测量。

items.stem: What do the new research findings suggest about mental health benefits?

choices.text: They can be easily seen among participants in a healthy weight range.
choices.zh: 它们可以在体重处于健康范围的参与者中轻易观察到。

choices.text: They should be attributed to participants' change in diet behaviors.
choices.zh: 它们应归因于参与者饮食行为的改变。

choices.text: They are linked to cooking confidence and cooking satisfaction.
choices.zh: 它们与烹饪信心和烹饪满意度相关。

choices.text: They actually result from eating more fruits and vegetables.
choices.zh: 它们实际上源于摄入更多水果和蔬菜。

items.stem: What plays a role in determining who benefits most from learning to cook?

choices.text: Gender.
Confidence.
Health.
Practice.

items.stem: What does research show about our personal space?

choices.text: It keeps others away.
It causes discomfort.
It remains visible.
It varies in size.

items.stem: What happens if a mere acquaintance enters our intimate space?

choices.text: It makes us feel uncomfortable.
It renders the acquaintance a stranger.
choices.zh: 它使这个熟人变成陌生人。

choices.text: It brings the acquaintance closer to us.
choices.zh: 它使这个熟人与我们更亲近。

choices.text: It causes the bubble around us to vanish.
choices.zh: 它导致我们周围的气泡消失。

items.stem: Where do people feel comfortable interacting with new acquaintances or strangers?

choices.text: In personal space.
In social space.
Within a distance of 18 inches.
Over 2 feet away from one another.
choices.zh: 在相互距离超过2英尺的地方。

items.stem: When are the sizes of our bubbles fixed?

choices.text: When we begin to feel fear.
choices.zh: 当我们开始感到恐惧时。

choices.text: When we develop a sense of space.
choices.zh: 当我们形成空间意识时。

choices.text: When we are 3 or 4 years old.
When we enter our teens.
choices.zh: 当我们进入青少年时期时。
